scope: Local Docker self-hosted rolling target (honua-yarp-rolling) on Docker Desktop for Windows. The server launches replicas, swaps its embedded proxy, keeps the prior replica through the observation window, runs the telemetry and golden-query gates and the recovery fence. The honua-devops executors run against the same server. Not AWS ECS-small, not the finding-driven proposal and approval path, not Console.

adaptations: Windows host: boot.sh takes PROOF_DOCKER_CLI (the Linux docker 27 CLI copied from docker:27-cli) because the host CLI is a Windows binary, and runs with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1. Restarts reproduce boot.sh start_server argument for argument from Python (restart.py) instead of a POSIX shell.

Deploy parameters add rollback.functional_query.path=/golden and rollback.functional_query.expected_contains = "revision": "prior-a". Since honua-server#3892 (in 93cad86, not in the 80e23be receipt) an automatic rollback completes only after a functional query proves the restored replica. A first run without them left every recovery cell at RollbackRequested with reason rollback.awaiting_data_plane and functionalQuery=NotProven.

Cell wrong-body-regression-satisfiable added. The original wrong-body-regression cell sets telemetry.golden_query.expected_contains and forbidden_contains to the same marker. Those keys also bind the restored-replica proof, so its recovery can never be proven; it settled Failed (rollback.functional_query_failed) after the 300-second window. The added cell uses a satisfiable expectation.
DevOps tests: the same two parameters and the Python restart in ProtectedRecoveryLiveJourneyTests; no other change.
